headline: Wattimena knocks out Littler 10-8; Price and Springer go through
standfirst: Jermaine Wattimena ended Luke Littler's Grand Slam defence in the last 16, and Gerwyn Price, Niko Springer and Kevin Doets also won through in Wolverhampton.
body: Jermaine Wattimena ended Luke Littler's defence of the Grand Slam of Darts on Wednesday night, beating the world number one 10-8 in the last 16 at Wolverhampton. The Dutchman, the 16th seed, had lost to Littler 16-2 when they met in this event in 2024 but this time earned a deserved victory.

Wattimena took the first interval with a 3-2 lead, added a 64 checkout and then produced a 12-darter to move 5-2 ahead. Six legs in a row became a 7-2 advantage, but missed doubles let Littler back in. The champion closed to 9-7 with a ten-darter and to 9-8 after another leg, only for Wattimena to hold firm and finish on 77. He plays Kevin Doets in the quarter-finals. Wattimena, visibly emotional afterwards, said that Littler is not unbeatable. Before the match, his friend Doets had told him to picture one of their own semi-finals rather than settle for winning two or three legs.

Doets, making his debut in the event, beat Cameron Menzies 10-5 with an average above 101. He missed double 12 for a nine-darter early on, took the first break of throw for 6-4 and then pulled away, finishing on double four.

Gerwyn Price, chasing a fourth Grand Slam title, beat Ryan Searle 10-7 and averaged 103.31. Checkouts of 148 and 147 helped him to leads of 4-1 and 5-3, and a 91 left him 6-4 ahead at the interval. Searle pulled back to 7-6 behind, but an 87 finish from Price made it 9-6 and he saw the game out.

Niko Springer was the first player into the quarter-finals, beating Rob Cross 10-8. The pair were level at 5-5 before Springer won five legs in a row to lead 9-5. Cross won three straight to get within a leg and survived a match dart, but Springer took out 111 to reach a first PDC Premier Event quarter-final.

Price now meets Springer in the last eight. The other half of the last 16 is played on Thursday, when Gabriel Clemens plays Nathan Aspinall, Gian van Veen faces Martin Schindler, Luke Humphries meets Tom Sykes and James Wade plays Michael van Gerwen.
